title: Immutable event sentinel for admin-audit and residency reporting
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: Legal and enterprise customers require cryptographically verifiable, region-aware audit records for admin actions, access events, and configuration changes. Current audit capture is robust but lacks an end-to-end verifier and residency manifest that can be used to produce automated attestation bundles for compliance audits. This ticket implements an 'Immutable Event Sentinel' — a lightweight service and data format that: 1) ingests admin audit events, 2) produces append-only chunk files with embedded integrity metadata, 3) publishes residency-aware manifests and periodic attestation bundles, and 4) integrates with the existing object storage retention features (S3 Object Lock + retention manifests) and HSM timestamping hooks.
scope: In scope: admin-actor events, privileged API calls, role/permission changes, console-based config edits, Dedicated/Private control-plane events. Produce immutable chunk artifacts, per-region residency manifest, attestation bundle generator, verification CLI, and console UI to surface attestations. Out of scope: telemetry-level app traces, user-generated content storage, migration of historical events older than 90 days (separate migration ticket).
goals: 1) Create an append-only chunk format (.aes) with event hashes + merkle roots and compact index. 2) Emit per-region residency manifests that map chunks to storage bucket+retention policy. 3) Provide an attestation bundle that includes signed manifests and proof-of-existence timestamps from KMS/HSM. 4) Verification command to validate a bundle against stored chunks. 5) Console surfaces: last-attestation time, manifest hash, retention policy enforcement status.
non_goals: 1) Replace full audit pipeline (we'll ingest from existing stream). 2) Implement legal escrow integrations (separate legal/escrow epic). 3) Rework retention enforcement mechanism — we will orchestrate current S3 retention APIs rather than reimplementing retention enforcement.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- Chunking cadence: default 1 hour or 100k events, whichever comes first. Smaller chunks improve granular audits but increase object count; we chose a hybrid cap to balance list/read costs.
- Indexing: include compact time + offset index in each chunk for fast forensic reads; avoid full event DB duplication.
- Integrity primitives: SHA-256 per event, Merkle root per chunk, and chunk-level signature using service KMS key. We avoid per-event signatures for cost reasons.
- Timestamping: first rely on KMS sign+system time; optionally append HSM notarization for enterprise customers via a background anchoring job.
- Retention modelling: publish residency manifest as a signed JSON with canonical sort order to prevent ambiguity instead of embedding policy metadata in object tags (tags are mutable).
acceptance_criteria: Chunks produced from the audit ingestion pipeline are written to region-specific buckets within 60 seconds of chunk close.
Each chunk contains per-event SHA-256 hashes, a Merkle root, compact index, and is signed by the sentinel service KMS key.
Residency manifest is generated and committed for every closed chunk and is signed; manifest includes bucket, object path, retention expiry, and canonical manifest hash.
Attestation bundle generator can produce a single downloadable .attest file for a given date range that includes signed manifests and proof-of-existence timestamps.
Verification CLI/tool accepts a .attest bundle and validates against objects in storage, returning PASS/FAIL with a short reason and list of mismatches.
Console UI shows last attestation time, manifest hash, and a link to download the attestation bundle for the selected region and date range.
Integration test coverage for chunk creation, manifest generation, attestation generation, and verification (unit+integration).
Metrics and alerts: missing-chunk >5% in a region, attestation-generation-failure rate >1% over 1h, verification failures >0 for released bundles.
Security review completed and design signed off by Security team (ticket attached).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Implement chunk format and local signer; wire up extractor that pulls admin events from existing audit stream and writes test chunks to a dev bucket.
Phase 2 (2 weeks): Implement residency manifest builder + KMS signing; add chunk upload with retention metadata (use Object Lock compliance mode where available) and canonical manifest generation.
Phase 3 (1 week): Attestation bundle generator and verification CLI; add unit/integration tests.
Phase 4 (1 week): Console surface work (small UI card + download link) and telemetry/alerts; e2e QA with sample enterprise tenant.
Phase 5 (1 week): Rollout to staging, smoke test across regions, run security review, enable for pilot customers, and document runbook.
monitoring_and_rollout: Rollout: feature-flag gated; enable for internal tenants first, then pilot customers, then company-wide in phases over 2 weeks.
Runbook: steps to re-run attestation generation, steps to recover missing chunks (if upload failed), and guidance to notify customers.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Large object counts increase S3 LIST costs. Mitigation: chunking hybrid cadence and lifecycle rollups to consolidated monthly archives for older data.
Risk: Retention metadata mismatch across regions. Mitigation: signed manifests + nightly manifest reconcilier job and alerting on parity diffs.

Risk: Verification false negatives due to eventual consistency. Mitigation: verification CLI will retry reads with exponential backoff and document expected read-after-write windows for each cloud provider.
Risk: Key compromise for signing key. Mitigation: rotate KMS key per quarter and provide revocation info in attestation bundle; enterprise customers can opt into customer-managed keys.
test_plan: Unit tests for chunk writer, manifest generator, and signer.
Integration test that ingests synthetic admin events, creates chunks, uploads to a test bucket with Object Lock enabled, generates attestation bundle, and verifies via CLI.
Performance test: create 1M events/day and validate chunking, upload throughput, and attestation generation within 2 hours for daily bundles.
Chaos test: simulate chunk upload failures and validate alerting + retry/reconciliation path.
